design_rationale: The study is a randomized controlled trial in which participants were assigned to treatment groups using central telephone randomization with sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes in a 2:1 ratio.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were blinded using sham skin incisions, a standardized postoperative pain medication protocol was adhered to, and analysis was conducted on an intention-to-treat basis with minimal protocol deviations.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the primary outcome (postoperative pain scores) and secondary outcomes were available for nearly all participants, with very low and balanced attrition across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the women in the study who received surgery 95.8% (92/96) of the adjustable single-incision sling group and 94.1% (48/51) of the transobturator sling group attended the 12-month follow-up visit, as is presented in our flowchart of the study (Fig. 2).

domain_judgments.rationale: The visual analog scale for pain was assessed identically in both groups by blinded participants (sham incisions used) and evaluated by independent assessors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was postoperative pain. Blinding of women was secured by not informing them on the randomization result before the procedure until 6 weeks postoperatively and by the additional use of two small (2-mm) sham “incisions” in the groin... domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered in the Netherlands Trial Register (NTR: 2558), and results for pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes are fully reported according to a pre-defined protocol.

This was assessed with a 100-mm visual analog scale at 1 and 2 hours after awakening... and thereafter subsequently daily for the first 3 days and weekly for 6 weeks.

overall_summary: The trial was judged to have a low risk of bias across all five domains due to concealed randomization, effective participant blinding via sham incisions, high follow-up rates, independent outcome assessment, and prospective registration with complete outcome reporting.

design_rationale: The study is described as a prospective randomized controlled trial where eligible patients were randomized via an envelope technique to either Needleless surgery or TOT.

domain_judgments.rationale: While opaque envelopes were used by non-surgical lab assistants, the exact sequence generation method is not specified, and envelopes were simply drawn from a batch of 200 rather than sequentially numbered, sealed, and concealed in a standard manner.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: group assignments were made and the surgical methods were selected via random selection of opaque labelingenvelope by lab assistant (a total of 200 envelopes, 100 for group A, 100 for group B, group A performing needleless surgery, group B performing TOT surgery). domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of patients and surgeons was not possible due to the nature of surgery, all randomized participants received their assigned intervention according to protocol, and there were no deviations from intended surgical interventions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear complete with all 368 randomized patients accounted for at the 12-month follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients received 12 months’ follow-up, and the patients from Ajust and TVT-O groups had no statistically significant difference in the subjective cure rate (94.4 vs 90.7 %, P = 0.171), as shown in Table 2.

domain_judgments.rationale: Appropriate measurement tools were used and outcome assessors were blinded to the surgical approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Scale filling and VAS measurement were conducted by trained professionals, and they were blinded to the surgical approaches.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-trial registration or published protocol is cited to confirm that all prespecified analyses and endpoints were reported without selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was the subjective cure (defined as ‘ ‘very much improved’ ’ or ‘ ‘much improved’ ’ on the PGI-I scale) at 12 months after surgery. The secondary endpoints were as follows: Objective cure...

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to an absence of information on allocation concealment during randomization and lack of a registered trial protocol to rule out selective reporting.
